title: O God, My Helper, Ever Near
description: O God, My Helper, Ever Near in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Fawcett wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 891 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"He holdeth our soul in life."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, my help-er, ev-er near! Crown with thy smile the pre-sent year; Pre-serve me by thy fa-vor still, And fit me for thy sa-cred will.

lines: O God, my helper, ever near!
Crown with thy smile the present year;
Preserve me by thy favor still,
And fit me for thy sacred will.
Accept my thanks for mercies past,
And be my guard, while life shall last.
My moments move with wingéd haste,
Nor know I which shall be the last:
Danger and death are ever nigh,
And I this year perhaps may die.
Prepare me for the trying day;
Then call my willing soul away:
I'll quit the world at thy command,
And trust my spirit to thy hand.

licence: Public domain: John Fawcett died in 1817.
credits: Words by John Fawcett (1740–1817), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
